title: ASML's Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography and the Limits of Reverse Engineering in China
gist: After the U.S. Commerce Department told ASML in June 2026 it suspects an EUV lithography machine reached China, the authors argue physical access buys far less than assumed: the binding constraint is tacit systems-integration knowledge across ~700,000 parts from ~5,000 suppliers, plus a co-developed consumables ecosystem (Tokyo Electron at ~100% of EUV coaters, Lasertec's actinic mask inspection near-monopoly) and ~10,000 embedded ASML service engineers. They conclude China cannot replicate EUV in a policy-relevant timeframe and that leapfrogging to accelerator-based or steady-state microbunching light sources is Beijing's most rational bet.

themes.theme: The Smuggling Allegation and What Access Actually Buys

insights.claim: In June 2026 the U.S. Department of Commerce informed ASML it suspects one of its extreme ultraviolet lithography machines has reached China, an accusation ASML denied and for which no supporting evidence has been made public.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: An unproven allegation is already driving export-control policy — headline risk for ASML without confirmed diversion.
insights.locator: In June, the U.S. Department of Commerce informed

insights.claim: Access to an EUV machine can accelerate component- and subsystem-level learning and reveal architectural choices, but cannot transfer systems-integration knowledge, accumulated trial-and-error experience, supplier relationships, or the maintenance capability needed to operate it at competitive performance and scale.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: The core investment thesis: ASML's moat is process knowledge, not hardware secrecy, so a leaked tool does not compress its lead.
insights.locator: Whereas this concern is legitimate, there are important constraints

insights.claim: In December 2025 former ASML engineers working for a Chinese lab reportedly helped produce an EUV lithography prototype by reverse-engineering older machines and studying their components.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: Talent flight is the live channel of technology transfer — watch retention policy and non-compete enforcement in the Netherlands.
insights.locator: Similar concerns emerged in December 2025

themes.theme: ASML's Position at the Leading Edge

insights.claim: ASML, founded in 1984 as a Philips spinoff, is the sole global producer of the machines capable of making the most advanced microchips and functions as a critical bottleneck for the AI revolution.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: Single-point dependency for the entire AI compute buildout — any ASML disruption propagates to every advanced node.
insights.locator: Born in 1984 as a spinoff from the Dutch electronics company Philips

insights.claim: For chips at five nanometers and below — the nodes used for the most advanced AI accelerators — no current alternative to ASML's machines exists.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: Defines exactly where the monopoly binds: sub-5nm logic, which is where AI accelerator demand is concentrated.
insights.locator: At the leading edge, its position is unrivalled.

insights.claim: SMIC's use of older deep ultraviolet machines with multi-patterning to make seven-nanometer chips is economically inefficient, hard to scale, raises defect rates, and becomes progressively less competitive at five-nanometer-class nodes and below.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: SMIC's 7nm workaround is a yield-and-cost dead end, not a path to competitive leading-edge supply — discount headlines about Chinese node parity.
insights.locator: It is true that for seven-nanometer chips the Chinese firm

insights.claim: An EUV machine costs on the order of $180 million, with the newest high-numerical-aperture machines running roughly $380 million.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: Hard ASP anchors for modelling ASML revenue mix as High-NA units replace standard EUV in the order book.
insights.locator: This massive complexity explains the cost

insights.claim: An EUV system comprises over 100,000 components at the system level and roughly 700,000 once subsystem parts are counted, sourced from about 5,000 suppliers including Zeiss mirrors and Trumpf lasers.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: Quantifies the replication problem and identifies Zeiss and Trumpf as the two most strategically exposed private suppliers.
insights.locator: An extreme ultraviolet system is composed of over 100,000 components

insights.claim: The central challenge of EUV is not building any individual component but making each perform inside a tightly coupled system whose other parts generate heat, vibration, contamination, and electromagnetic interference.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: A generalizable rule for assessing any hardware moat: integration difficulty, not component difficulty, determines defensibility.
insights.locator: The central challenge is making sure that each of these components

insights.claim: Systems integration in EUV is closer to art than codified science, with most of the required knowledge accumulated over decades through repeated testing, production failures, supplier interactions, and debugging inside ASML and its suppliers.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: Tacit knowledge cannot be stolen, subsidized, or reverse-engineered on a schedule — the strongest argument that ASML's lead is durable.
insights.quote: Such systems integration, however, is closer to art than to codified science.
insights.locator: Such systems integration, however, is closer to art

insights.claim: EUV machines must hold sub-atomic tolerances continuously for months of uninterrupted high-volume operation, with disturbances as mundane as vibrations from passing traffic capable of pushing them out of tolerance.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: Illustrates why fab siting, foundations, and environmental control are non-trivial cost drivers in any new leading-edge fab.
insights.locator: Making matters harder, the machine must hold these margins

insights.claim: EUV subsystem specifications are extreme in absolute terms: a laser striking tin droplets roughly 50,000 times per second to generate plasma about forty times hotter than the sun's surface, and mirrors polished to picometer precision that scaled to Germany's area would deviate by one-tenth of a millimeter.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: Concrete engineering thresholds any would-be competitor must clear before integration even becomes the problem.
insights.locator: The discussion in the media about ASML has focused primarily

insights.claim: ASML co-develops components with roughly 5,000 specialized supplier firms, supplying technical specifications and refining them until a working equilibrium is reached, making the supplier relationship itself part of the technology.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: Supplier co-development means the moat extends across corporate boundaries and cannot be replicated by a vertically integrated national champion.
insights.locator: ASML co-develops them with these specialized firms

themes.theme: Why China Cannot Copy on a Policy-Relevant Timeline

insights.claim: Industrial espionage, reverse engineering, and talent poaching can reveal architectural choices and accelerate a particular subsystem, but cannot supply the tacit, path-dependent process knowledge distributed across countless engineers in multiple organizations and countries that ensures commercially viable yield, reliability, and throughput.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: Core contrarian call against the assumption that a stolen tool collapses the export-control regime's value.
insights.locator: Industrial espionage, reverse engineering, and talent poaching can reveal

insights.claim: China has so far failed to catch up not only in EUV but also in the previous generation of immersion deep ultraviolet machines dating from the late 2000s.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: The strongest empirical evidence in the piece: a nearly 20-year-old technology remains unreplicated, calibrating expectations for EUV.
insights.locator: And in fact, China has so far failed to catch up

insights.claim: China is not going to mass-produce EUV machines any time soon: with 5 units scheduled for delivery in 2026 to multiple semiconductor producers, the machines are still at the development stage.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: A falsifiable near-term marker — five development units in 2026 is the number to track against mass-production claims.
insights.quote: with 5 units scheduled for delivery in 2026 to multiple semiconductor producers, the machines are still at the development stage
insights.locator: In contrast to some recent reactions

insights.claim: Because EUV capability improves through accumulated operating experience and ASML has already introduced a high-numerical-aperture generation, China risks chasing a moving target while still struggling to master earlier generations.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: Experience-curve dynamics mean the gap widens with time unless the entrant leapfrogs — supports long-duration ASML pricing power.
insights.quote: China might be chasing a moving target as it struggles to master earlier generations
insights.locator: Because extreme ultraviolet capability improves through accumulated operating experience

insights.claim: A fully functioning EUV scanner cannot produce a single leading-edge chip on its own; it depends on a highly concentrated ecosystem of materials and equipment.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: Redirects attention from the scanner to the consumables layer, where several under-followed monopolies sit.
insights.locator: A fully functioning extreme ultraviolet lithography machine cannot produce

insights.claim: Qualified EUV photoresists for high-volume manufacturing come predominantly from a small group of Japanese-headquartered companies including JSR, Tokyo Ohka Kogyo, and Shin-Etsu Chemical, with Lam Research and Dongjin Semichem pursuing alternatives.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: Names a specific Japanese materials oligopoly that is both an investable niche and a sanctions chokepoint.
insights.locator: Qualified resists for high-volume manufacturing

insights.claim: Tokyo Electron holds essentially 100 percent of the market for extreme ultraviolet photoresist coaters and developers.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: A second de facto monopoly alongside ASML in the EUV stack — comparable strategic leverage, far less policy attention.
insights.quote: Tokyo Electron holds essentially 100 percent of the market for extreme ultraviolet photoresist coaters and developers.
insights.locator: The coaters and developers that apply and process the photoresist

insights.claim: Mask blanks, the defect-free reflective substrates on which circuit patterns are written, are made by only two or three companies worldwide including Hoya and AGC.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: Another two-to-three-supplier chokepoint with concentrated pricing power and severe single-point supply risk.
insights.locator: Mask blanks, the defect-free reflective substrates

insights.claim: KLA leads the broad process-control market while Lasertec holds a near-monopoly on actinic mask-inspection tools operating at the same 13.5-nanometer wavelength as EUV.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: Lasertec's actinic inspection monopoly is explicitly named as a control-worthy chokepoint — a policy risk and a moat simultaneously.
insights.locator: Extreme ultraviolet-grade metrology and inspection is similarly concentrated.

insights.claim: Because photoresist, mask blanks, and tin purity are all co-developed and specified to a particular machine over years at atomic-scale tolerances, China reproducing the scanner would face the integration problem a second time across the entire consumables chain.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: Doubles the replication cost estimate: scanner plus a matched consumables ecosystem, each requiring years of joint tuning.
insights.locator: China is of course trying to develop its own supplier ecosystem.

insights.claim: A new photoresist must satisfy partly conflicting requirements across resolution, sensitivity, and line-edge roughness plus stringent defectivity and outgassing standards, and undergo extensive qualification with the exposure tool and surrounding coating, development, etching, and inspection processes before adoption.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: Explains the switching-cost mechanism that locks incumbent materials suppliers in for years — a durable revenue characteristic.
insights.locator: Replacing an established supplier is difficult

themes.theme: Service Dependency as a Kill Switch

insights.claim: ASML embeds roughly 10,000 customer-support engineers inside customers' fabs worldwide working twelve-hour shifts day and night, described by one ASML executive as the company's front-line troops.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: A 10,000-person embedded service base is both recurring high-margin revenue and a de facto operational kill switch over any installed tool.
insights.quote: what one ASML executive describes as the company’s “front-line troops.”
insights.locator: ASML embeds a workforce of roughly 10,000 customer-support engineers

insights.claim: An EUV system must be continuously calibrated and depends on an uninterrupted flow of spare parts, software updates, and hands-on servicing from ASML, so a smuggled machine degrades without vendor support.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: Service cutoff is a more reliable enforcement tool than physical interdiction — the real teeth in the export-control regime.
insights.locator: Setting production aside, there remains the problem of keeping the machine running.

insights.claim: An ASML customer-support engineer trains for close to a year rotating through centers in Taiwan, the United States, and Germany before being cleared to work unsupervised, and diagnosis is often embodied and intuitive — one engineer caught an incipient failure by feeling a barely perceptible distortion in a cooling hose.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: Concretizes why service capability cannot be transferred with hardware — a year of embodied training per engineer.
insights.locator: A customer-support engineer trains for close to a year

themes.theme: Policy Levers and the Leapfrog Risk

insights.claim: Talent is the critical bottleneck in China's EUV effort, so allied governments should build retention and counter-recruitment programs to restrict access to critical individuals even at the component and subsystem level.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: Signals a coming policy front in personnel restrictions that would affect hiring and mobility across the semiconductor equipment sector.
insights.locator: First, talent is a critical bottleneck.

insights.claim: Every one of the hundreds of thousands of components in an EUV system is both a point of failure and a point of leverage, so controls should be calibrated at chokepoints like actinic mask-inspection tools and photoresists to force Chinese espionage and research efforts to disperse.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: Flags specific sub-components most likely to face the next round of export controls — actionable for supply-chain exposure mapping.
insights.locator: Second, a system of hundreds of thousands of components

insights.claim: Western governments should deliberately induce Chinese engineers and scientists to spend scarce effort on copying technologies that cannot in practice be reproduced, because espionage is not free and imposes trade-offs.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: An unusual offensive framing — the value of a leaked machine may be negative for China if it diverts scarce talent.
insights.quote: if China is determined to copy, Western governments have an interest in ensuring it spends its effort copying rather than building the accumulated experience that catching up actually requires
insights.locator: Third, China’s drive to acquire foreign technology

insights.claim: Because recreating EUV is so difficult, leapfrogging to a next-generation technology where no incumbent has an advantage is China's most rational bet, with alternative light sources based on particle accelerators and steady-state microbunching already under investigation at Tsinghua University and moving from lab demonstration toward a dedicated facility.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: The genuine long-term threat to ASML is not a copied scanner but an alternative light source that resets the experience curve — a specific technology to monitor.
insights.locator: Fourth, because recreating this capability is so difficult

insights.claim: Accelerator-based and steady-state microbunching light sources would sidestep the tin-droplet plasma source ASML and Cymer spent years perfecting, and although none is close to displacing EUV today, each resets the experience curve on which ASML's lead depends.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: Identifies the precise mechanism by which ASML's moat could be neutralized — obsoleting the accumulated experience rather than copying it.
insights.locator: None of these are close to displacing these machines today

insights.claim: Allied governments should treat frontier lithography alternatives, not just existing chokepoints, as a domain of competition and work to lock China out of them early.
insights.speaker: Andrea Gilli, Mauro Gilli, Francesco Fimiani, and Nicolas Deriquehem
insights.so_what: Anticipates export controls extending to pre-commercial research areas, broadening compliance scope for universities and labs.
insights.locator: Allied governments should therefore treat frontier alternatives
